payload.rationale: August 2026 housing starts were 1.275 million, slightly below the 1.300M threshold, while July was 1.309 million. However, August building permits, a leading indicator, were notably higher at 1.394 million, suggesting a pipeline that could easily push September starts above 1.300M. The month-to-month volatility of housing starts is high (margin of error +/- 12%), meaning a small bounce back is quite plausible. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is the recent sharp increase in 30-year fixed mortgage rates, which rose from 6.65% in late August to 6.95% by mid-September; this could rapidly cool builder confidence and delay groundbreakings. The strongest reason it could be too low is that the strong permit numbers from August might translate directly into September starts regardless of the recent mortgage rate uptick, as financing for those projects may have already been secured.
limitations: High volatility in month-to-month housing starts data.
Mortgage rates are changing rapidly, and their immediate impact on September starts is uncertain.
August data is preliminary and subject to revision.
